subject: is there a way to get the estimated rates from a poisson model with offset

messages.author: 7d1ac766483df74a
messages.subject: is there a way to get the estimated rates from a poisson model with offset
parts:
Using this simple example:

dat = data.table(
    id = c(1:8),
    deaths = c(5, 30, 2, 4, 5, 4, 7, 10),
    pop = c(1000, 2300, 300, 400, 500, 700, 1000, 700)
)

result = inla(deaths ~ 1, family = "poisson", data = dat, 
    offset = log(pop),
    control.compute=list(config = TRUE))

summary(result)
Call:
   c("inla(formula = deaths ~ 1, family = \"poisson\", data = dat, offset
   = log(pop), ", " control.compute = list(config = TRUE))")
Time used:
    Pre = 0.579, Running = 0.244, Post = 0.0249, Total = 0.849
Fixed effects:
              mean    sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode kld
(Intercept) -4.635 0.122     -4.883   -4.632     -4.403 -4.626   0

Marginal log-Likelihood:  -20.34
Posterior summaries for the linear predictor and the fitted values are computed
(Posterior marginals needs also 'control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE)')

The average rate would be exp(-4.635) = 0.0097. Is there a way to get those fitted values using result$summary.linear.predictor?

Thanks, 
Sebastian

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] is there a way to get the estimated rates from a poisson model with offset
parts:
I think you’re looking for $summary.fitted.values, that is like summary.linear predictor but after applying the link function (or it’s inverse, exp).
( For this to work on plain predictions you also need to set link=1 in one of the control.* options; not at my computer to check which one at the moment.)

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] is there a way to get the estimated rates from a poisson model with offset
parts:
If you just want the transformation of the intercept, use the inla.tmarginal() and/or inla.emarginal etc functions on the marginals.fixed output (if it’s not there you may need to turn them on; the last lines of your output mentions that for some of the marginals, but I thing the fixed effects marginals are there anyway).

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] is there a way to get the estimated rates from a poisson model with offset
parts:
…and remember that E(exp(x)) is not equal to exp(E(x)). Only the quantiles transform in that way, so for posterior mean of exp(x) you can use inla.emarginal to compute the correct, first expression.

Finn
